live_web_research.page_text: YFQ-44A Completes Second Exercise with the Experimental Operations Unit - MilitaryLeak.COM Skip to content × × Home Aerial Warfare YFQ-44A Completes Second Exercise with the Experimental Operations Unit YFQ-44A Completes Second Exercise with the Experimental Operations Unit The U.S. Air Force’s Experimental Operations Unit (EOU) is focused on putting operational Air Force personnel in the loop early, enabling the experimentation with concepts of employment, mission planning, logistics, and sustainment required to accelerate operational fielding of Collaborative Combat Aircraft. Four months ago, EOU operators launched, recovered, and sustained YFQ-44A for the first time, an important step in taking CCA from prototype to credible combat capability. Last month, during our second exercise with the EOU at Creech Air Force Base, we took the next steps down the path to operational fielding of production FQ-44 fighters. The exercise increased the task complexity and expanded the responsibilities owned by Air Force personnel. EOU operators tasked the aircraft throughout the various stages of mission execution from multiple locations, demonstrating the disaggregated control required to reduce manpower requirements and turn CCA sorties from austere bases. Operational users also directly oversaw daily mission autonomy flights with YFQ-44A for the first time, using mission autonomy to execute operationally-relevant tactics and maneuvers throughout the event. The exercise built on the foundation established at the first EOU exercise in April, once again showcasing how YFQ-44A is simple to operate, maintain, and sustain. A week of on-time, high-tempo flight operations — including multiple days with multiple sorties per day — is a testament to both the maturity of the aircraft and EOU operators’ increasing familiarity with the system. This latest EOU exercise is tangible evidence that the operational procedures and trust required to field FQ-44 at scale are taking shape. Regular testing and experimentation with operational end users is central to how the CCA program will deliver a combat credible capability quickly. The event marked the first of the thousands of sorties that prototype YFQ-44A and production FQ-44 semi-autonomous fighter aircraft will fly out of Creech in the coming years, adding to the legacy of an installation that has been at the center of the Air Force’s uncrewed aircraft enterprise for decades. Anduril Industries look forward to deepening collaboration Air Force operators in every exercise still yet to come, each of which represents an important step on the pathway from prototype to operational capability. live_web_research.page_text: YFQ-44A uncrewed fighter completes second Air Force exercise - Military Embedded Systems YFQ-44A uncrewed fighter completes second Air Force exercise Share on X Share on LinkedIn News August 19, 2026 Dan Taylor Technology Editor Military Embedded Systems YFQ-44A via Anduril CREECH AIR FORCE BASE, Nevada. Anduril's YFQ-44A Collaborative Combat Aircraft prototype completed a second exercise with the U.S. Air Force Experimental Operations Unit (EOU), expanding Air Force personnel involvement in mission execution and autonomy testing, the company announced in a statement. During the exercise, EOU personnel tasked the aircraft from multiple locations and oversaw daily mission-autonomy flights, the statement reads. The testing included operational tactics and maneuvers and was intended to evaluate distributed control concepts that could reduce personnel requirements for Collaborative Combat Aircraft operations, the company says. The event followed an earlier exercise in April in which Air Force personnel launched, recovered, and sustained the YFQ-44A. The latest testing included multiple sorties on some days and is part of preparations for production FQ-44 semi-autonomous aircraft operations at Creech Air Force Base, according to the statement. Several weeks after Anduril officially unveiled the YFQ-44A in Ohio , the new combat drone has completed its second exercise with experimental units from the U.S. Air Force (USAF) at Creech Air Force Base, Nevada. The activity expanded the responsibilities assigned to operational personnel and marked another step in preparing the system for future Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) operations. 👉 Read more: First Tamir missile interceptor built entirely in the U.S. is delivered to Israel The exercise was conducted by the Experimental Operations Unit (EOU), which was established to integrate operational personnel into the early stages of the program. Its objective is to test employment concepts, mission planning, logistics and sustainment before the CCAs move toward operational deployment. YFQ-44A – US Air Force – Anduril YFQ-44A expands its role during the exercise During this second exercise, EOU operators assumed greater responsibility across different stages of mission execution. Personnel controlled the aircraft from multiple locations, an approach intended to reduce manpower requirements and enable CCA operations from bases with limited infrastructure. 📌 You may also like Montana ends C-130H operations as the U.S. Air National Guard continues transition to C-130J Lockheed Martin integrates U.S. Army NGC2 capabilities across four mission threads Operational users also supervised daily autonomous mission flights involving the YFQ-44A for the first time. This capability allowed the system to execute tactics and maneuvers associated with operational scenarios, helping evaluate its performance under more complex employment conditions. The exercise also tested the operators’ ability to sustain a high operational tempo. Scheduled flight operations were conducted over the course of a week, with multiple days involving more than one sortie, while personnel continued to build familiarity with the new system. YFQ-44A – US Air Force – Anduril The CCA program moves toward Operational Capability The second exercise built on the results of the EOU’s first activity, which took place in April. During that event, operators participated for the first time in launching, recovering and sustaining the YFQ-44A, representing an important step toward transitioning the aircraft from the prototype stage to a future combat capability. The U.S. Air Force considers testing with operational users a central component of the CCA program. These exercises allow the service to develop and validate procedures before introducing production-standard FQ-44 aircraft on a larger scale. Creech Air Force Base is expected to play an important role in the program’s next phases. The installation was also where the drone underwent its initial operational testing last July . Thousands of sorties are expected to be conducted with the YFQ-44A prototypes and future FQ-44 semi-autonomous combat aircraft. The base already has extensive experience operating unmanned aircraft, including through the 432nd Wing, which operates the MQ-9A Reaper. YFQ-44A – US Air Force – Anduril The new YFQ-44A combat drone forms part of the Collaborative Combat Aircraft concept, which seeks to integrate uncrewed systems with crewed aircraft. The tests conducted at Creech will help further define the tactics, techniques and procedures required for the system’s eventual integration into the USAF’s operational force. * Images courtesy of Anduril. article.body:
YFQ-44A Completes Second Exercise with Air Force Experimental Operations Unit

Anduril announced on August 18 that its YFQ-44A completed a second exercise with the U.S. Air Force’s Experimental Operations Unit at Creech Air Force Base, Nevada. Air Force personnel tasked the aircraft from multiple locations and directly oversaw daily mission-autonomy flights for the first time during a week of operations with multiple sorties on some days. The exercise expanded operational-user responsibility beyond the first event in April. Further exercises with Air Force operators are planned.

Source: Anduril
